nodes.reason: Prose and exact type agree, including arbitrary support regions and dimensions. Equality on admissible forms gives mass scaling; the mass-support characterization and positive finite ENNReal cancellation then prove support and density invariance. No circular reliance.
The inclusion isometry, Hausdorff-volume identification, and Haar scaling establish precisely the stated normalization. The proof also covers n = 0; all hypotheses match the Lean proposition.

Outer regularity correctly extends the local open-set inequality to Borel pieces. Disjointification yields a uniform positive mass for every disc, contradicting finite mass on the common bounded ball. The dependency on subspace_ball_measure is correctly directed.

The first failure lies strictly between 0 and L. The backward sector satisfies the frozen endpoint lemma, hypothesis (ii) supplies local constant density, and two independent arc directions identify the local plane with Q. This closes the contradiction; L ≤ 0 is vacuous.

The proof supplies all intermediate obligations: integer densities and sufficient ambient dimension, a locally minimal jump value, accumulating light points, continued arcs, uniformly sized good discs, disjointness for distinct planes, and finite fibres. The resulting infinite family satisfies the finite-mass contradiction exactly, without assuming the parent classification.

The local-plane uniqueness and clopen great-circle argument are valid. Compactness gives finitely many distinct planes, intersections are reduced to the origin, and positive dilation covers every nonzero point of S. The empty-link case correctly permits q = 0.

Restriction preserves the required cycle, support, and mass properties. Connected punctured planes permit planar constancy; measure uniqueness extends the formula to Borel pieces. Null mass at the origin and off the planes then gives the constant integer density ratio, including q = 0. No cone or minimizing hypothesis is silently required.
